summary: Frontend-only regression and UI verification completed for opaque language-toggle refinement on public preview and snapshot baseline. Core geometry, opacity/material, SVG integrity, drag/click/keyboard flows, and byte-level static constraints passed.

Touch coverage completed in main-agent follow-up using CDP touch emulation; initial context limitation resolved.
critical_code_review_comments: All 66 HTML pages are byte-identical to /tmp/nova-toggle-before-opaque/frontend (0 diffs).
language-toggle.js is byte-identical to baseline; language-toggle-gesture.js and language CSS block changed as expected.
CSS before language-selector marker is byte-identical to baseline; only toggle block changed.

Knob is opaque in computed styles (background-color rgb(236,236,236), backdrop-filter none). Pixel check on central 11x11 area of knob screenshot between TR vs EN differs by <=1 RGB unit, indicating no underlying flag tint bleed in interior.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Executed pytest suites: 6/6 (lang toggle regression), 61/61 (serving modes), 98/98 (static pages). Browser automation on preview validated: 48x26 rail + 24x24 knob desktop, 32x20 rail + 18x18 knob narrow tablet, knob left/top 0 with 1px effective outer gaps, --lang-travel behavior via drag (~11px move produced ~11px knob translate), no navigation while held, release-to-commit endpoint behavior, click and keyboard navigation. Touchscreen-specific drag could not be directly simulated because hasTouch is disabled in this automation context.
rca of the issue: No product defect reproduced in this run. One apparent failure in first script was test-logic error (a 3px micro-move was interpreted as a tap, which intentionally toggles language by design). Reproduced with proper return-gesture (>4px move then return), nearest-endpoint commit worked correctly.
